To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed an inductively coupled plasma mass-spectrometry-based method to obtain specific quantification of the sulfenic acid (a redox-sensitive protein modification) in peptides and protein samples.
we have developed a robust method to obtain the specific quantification and absolute quantification (AQUA) of sulfenic acid residues in peptides and proteins by using ICPMS.
we present an inductively coupled plasma mass-spectrometry (ICPMS)-based method for the specific detection and quantification of sulfenylated peptides and proteins.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of ICPMS-based methods for the specific quantitation of sulfenic acid and thiols in peptides and proteins.
a new approach to the specific detection and quantification of sulfonic acids and thiol residues by ICPMS.
the development of new reagents to quantify sulfenic acids and thiols in peptides and proteins by ICPMS.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

ICPMS is a very powerful and versatile tool for the quantification of sulfenylated residues in peptides and proteins, and the presented approach can be used to monitor the thiol-SA redox equilibrium in various biological states and diseases.
the presented ICPMS-based methods allow for the first time to obtain specific and quantitative data on sulfenic acid in proteins.
this is the most robust and sensitive method for the determination of sulfenic acid and thiols.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the new method allows the specific quantification and characterization of SA in peptides and proteins and the simultaneous determination of thiols in the same samples.
ICPMS-based methods are a valuable addition to the toolbox of analytical methods for the quantification of SA in peptides and proteins.
the new ICPMS-based approach is a powerful analytical tool to study the thiol-sulfinic/sulphenic acid redox cycle in peptides and proteins.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ICPMS can be used to quantify SA in proteins and peptides.
ICPMS can be used to study the thiol-sulphenic acid equilibrium in biological systems.

the developed methodology can be used for the quantification of sulfenylated proteins and peptides in biological samples and for the determination of thiol and sulfenic acid redox equilibrium in proteins and peptides.
